main_text.p: poris: nisi quis malit wurthan hic idem sonare ac Sax. ʒepopȯen, id est, fieri: tunc autem verba sonant, adnihilabitur, sive, ad nihilum reducetur.

Fellon sal, Destruet: nos vellen dejiciet] Eodem sensu (proftrandi scil. sive dejiciendi) nobis to fell, ut in arbore proftrandâ, quod nobis to fell a tree, in bove malleo lanii proftrato, quod nobis felling an ore, & id genus aliis. Fluit autem à verbo faelen, cadere; quod enim sic dejicitur aut destruitur, non sine casu destruitur.
Ferterron sal, Perdes: nos verde-ruen: fertherttbu, perdas.
Fertwerthan sal, Peribit: fertwer-thet, Pereatis] Perire Sax. fopnpy̆n̆san.
Follelcten, Opitulentur] Adjuvare, opem ferre, Sax. fyl̆rtian, unde ful-tum pro adjutorium.
Fozsuoz, Prodiit] Huic affine nostratium fozth-fare, quod (ortu Saxonicum) & obitum, & corporis de loco obitus exportationem, funeris ergo, olim signabat.
Framsozitthu, Recessisti] Compositum reor à fram, nobis hodie from, Sax. autem fpam, i. e. à, ab, & faran, ire, transfire,

page.notes: Old-English/Saxon glosses in black letter and Greek and Hebrew-like characters are transcribed approximately; several Saxon words are doubtful and should be checked against the scan. Pencil marks "927" in the right margin are not printed text.
